title: A Rust test driving a whole call negotiation between two agents over JMAP
description:
Split out of bead mimid-1wgh.114.9 on 2026-11-23, and the half that
keeps the call work correct rather than the half that shows it off.

WHAT IT DOES. Two agents in process, as mimid-agent-jmap
tests/two_accounts.rs already sets up for chat, driven entirely through
the JMAP surface:
1. read each Session's urn:ietf:params:jmap:vtc capability: iceServers,
   supportsMimiCalls, and that the websocket capability is advertised;
2. alice creates a chat with bob, bob joins;
3. alice VTCCall/set create, callType "room", chatId the chat's: assert
   the VTCCall comes back with a mimiRoomId, and that the room it names
   is parent-dependent on the chat's room;
4. both open the JMAP WebSocket and send VTCStreamEnable;
5. alice VTCCall/signal an offer; ASSERT BOB RECEIVES A VTCCallSignal
   whose sdp is byte-identical to what alice sent, whose participantId
   is alice, and whose callId is the call;
6. bob answers; alice receives it, likewise byte-identical;
7. both send a candidate; ASSERT THE CANDIDATE OBJECT THAT ARRIVES
   EQUALS THE ONE SENT, field by field -- this is the assertion that
   would have caught the bug of 2026-11-23, where a candidate was sent
   with no payload at all and everything compiled, linted and passed;
8. VTCCall/exportMediaSecret on both sides: assert the same bytes and
   the same epoch, which is the keying claim of
   draft-atwood-mimi-calls proved over the wire rather than in the
   store.

WHY IT IS P1 AND THE PAGE IS NOT. Every layer between the store and a
client is new: the extension handler, the socket, the fragment codec,
the capability. A browser demo exercises all of them once, by hand, and
reports "no audio". This reports which one.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, and cannot: the media. No browser, no WebRTC, no
DTLS-SRTP. It proves the negotiation a call needs, not that a call
sounds like anything. That is bead mimid-1wgh.114.9's page.

NOTE ON THE ORACLE: step 7's assertion is on the candidate OBJECT, not
the SDP fragment the wire carries. The fragment is an implementation
detail of the agent's codec (vtc_backend::candidate_fragment and
vtc_stream::candidate_of); what a client is owed is the
RTCIceCandidateInit it gave back unchanged. Assert the contract, not the
encoding.
